title: Reconciliation
tomorrow: your table: who's supposed to sit at it, friends or strangers?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Joseph wept over his brothers and forgave them all over again: forgiveness as a decision that comes before the feeling. Decide first. Today, the half that needs two people.

Walking out in the middle of a service feels rude. Phones off, sit still, stay to the end. Yet in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus tells someone to leave mid-worship. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "If therefore thou offer thy gift at the altar, and there thou remember that thy brother hath any thing against thee; Leave there thy offering before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to thy brother." Read it twice, and something odd turns up. Whose grudge is it?
screen: `WALK OUT OF WORSHIP?` → `LEAVE THERE THY OFFERING.` → `WHOSE GRUDGE IS IT?`

segments.voice: Look at who's upset. Not the one at the altar. The brother has something against him. The verse doesn't say: if you're angry, go and forgive. It says: if someone else is holding a hurt, maybe one you think is unfair, you're the one who gets up and goes. That's the puzzle solved. Yesterday's forgiveness is a decision one person can make alone. Reconciliation takes two. It's the walk across the room, and Jesus hands that walk to the person at the altar. Then the verse ends: and then coming thou shalt offer thy gift. The worship isn't called off. It's put in order, the way you clear a table before you set it: first the people beside you, then the gift. One to tell a friend: Catholics act this out at Mass. Just before Communion, people turn and offer each other a sign of peace, and the Church's instructions place it there on purpose, peace with each other before receiving. Confession carries the word too; the Church calls it the sacrament of reconciliation. Going first doesn't promise the other person will meet you. Paul puts it carefully in his letter to the Romans: "If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men." Your half is the walk.
screen: `THE BROTHER HOLDS THE GRUDGE.` · `FORGIVE ALONE; RECONCILE IN TWOS.` · `THE SIGN OF PEACE BEFORE COMMUNION.` · `AS MUCH AS IS IN YOU.` · then, large: `GO FIRST.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who might have something against you. First, name what peace with them would look like. Then name what stops you: pride, fear, not knowing how to begin. Last, choose one small first step and when you'll take it, a message, a hello, a coffee. If you pray, you can ask for the nerve to walk across the room.
Reconciliation. Two people walking back toward each other after a rift, and someone has to take the first step. Today's word.
The line to keep: go first, and let the gift wait at the altar until you're back. Until tomorrow.

chat.says: now mia's upset i iced her out all week. SHE skipped my night. why do i go first?
options: Matthew 5: if she has something against you, you go. Going first isn't saying you're wrong.
You don't. Wait until she says sorry for being upset, and then you're even.
Only if you were wrong too. Otherwise it's her job to come to you first.
chat.meaning: Jesus sends the one at the altar to go first when the other person holds the grudge. Reconciliation is a walk across the room, not a verdict.
